_comment: Blanket whole-SN renumbering. Unlike strongs-location-overrides.json (one specific occurrence, keyed by book:chapter:verse:token_ordinal), each entry here applies to EVERY occurrence of the old number, corpus-wide, with no per-occurrence enumeration needed. Applied in applySnRenumber()/loadLexicons() in server.js. Format: "H<old>": { "to": "H<new>", "reason": "...", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "raw_root": "<optional paleo string>" }. raw_root (added 2026-08-24) is the OLD, actually-attested root spelling this renumber's canonical root (strongs-roots.json[to]) replaces — when present, canonicalizeRootSurface() in server.js splices the canonical root into every occurrence's displayed surface form (Root Explorer's Surface Forms list, Surfaces tab, occurrence lookups), not just the root header entry. Omit it for a renumber that's purely a relabeling (no root respelling involved).

H802.reason: H802 (אשה, "woman/wife") shared its root (𐤀𐤔𐤄, Ash+He) with H800/H801 (אש, "fire" / אשה, "offering by fire") in strongs-roots.json, so gloss lookups (keyed by paleo root, not SN) collided and H801 displayed H802's "woman" gloss. Root repointed to derive from H376 (איש, "ish"/man) plus the feminine he -- exactly matching H802's own Strong's derivation note, "feminine of H376" -- giving Ayashah (𐤀𐤉𐤔𐤄) instead of the old Ashah. fieldy: "the word derives from 376 and should be ayashah". Renumbered to H378a (not just re-rooted) because the app's root explorer sorts alphabetically by root spelling -- Ayashah now naturally lands between H378 (Ayashabashath) and H379 (Ayashahawad), inside Strong's own ish-family cluster (H376-H380), and 802 looked like a random leftover sitting there once the root moved. fieldy: "someone scanning 801->802->803 should allow a landing on 802 with a message" -- see the 410 tombstone response in GET /api/root-explorer/root.
